gaps.sentence: We'll be fine ___ the forecast is wrong.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless the forecast is wrong' = if it is not wrong.

gaps.sentence: If the taxi ___ in five minutes, we are going to miss our flight.
gaps.hint: real future risk in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Real future conditions take the present simple in the if-clause: does not arrive.

gaps.sentence: If the route ___ safer, I would cycle to work.
gaps.hint: an imaginary present situation, subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: Unreal present conditions formally take 'were' rather than 'is': were.

gaps.sentence: If you had set an alarm, you ___.
gaps.explanation: The present result of a past unreal condition takes 'would not be': would not still be asleep.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: If I ___ a million euros, I would travel the world for a year.
gaps.explanation: Second conditionals use the past simple after 'if' for unreal presents: won.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.

gaps.sentence: If plants ___ enough light, their leaves turn yellow.
gaps.hint: a general truth in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Zero conditionals state general truths with the present simple in both clauses: do not get.
